name: Rogers Electrical Contracting
old_description: Rogers Electrical is an electrical contracting company the specializes in Turn-Key electrical projects for various industrial and commercial customers. We have the team, tools, equipment and experience needed to be a viable asset to design and/or build a complete electrical system for any project. We work hard with our customers to achieve the goals that they have in mind and we can give ideas/advice to possible make an even better outcome.
about:
Rogers Electrical Contracting Company, Inc. was founded in 1996 and is headquartered in Fairmont, West Virginia. The firm operates additional divisions in Pennsylvania, Illinois, and North Carolina to serve industrial and commercial customers across the region.

The company provides turnkey electrical contracting services encompassing engineering and design, power line and substation construction, system automation and PLC/SCADA integration, control panel fabrication, fiber optic installation and testing, commercial electrical systems, and bore hole cable services for mining applications. Its in-house professional engineer and design team use CAD, ETAP, and PLS-CADD software to produce detailed project renderings, while an extensive equipment fleet enables work at remote job sites.

Rogers Electrical serves the aggregate, oil and gas, coal, water, and electric utility industries, as well as commercial construction. Notable projects include a turnkey upgrade of a coal preparation plant in Philippi, WV, involving electrical design, installation, programming, and start-up, and the design and build of a 50 MVA 138-34.5 kV substation for a mine power system in the same area.

The firm emphasizes its more than three decades of industry experience and a commitment to going the extra mile for quality. Its service model combines complete plant builds, plant upgrades, overland conveyor systems, motor control centers, and PLC programming under a single turnkey umbrella, aiming to make projects efficient and cost-effective.

name: Ron's Home Style Foods
old_description: At Rons Foods, we make our products fresh daily under USDA and FDA inspection with the highest quality ingredients and processes to ensure a homemade look and taste. The production facility exceeds all food safety expectations. Our attention to detail extends beyond what can be seen and tasted.
about:
Ron's Home Style Foods was founded in the spring of 1985 by Ron Woodall in Houston, Texas. The family-owned company began with a mission to produce high-quality, home-style deli salads that look and taste homemade. Woodall had previously developed the successful Ron's Krispy Fried Chicken chain before launching the venture.

Today the company operates a USDA- and FDA-inspected production facility where it makes deli salads, dips and spreads, dressings and bases, gourmet burger kits, frozen sides and entrees, and provides co-packing and private-label services. Products are prepared fresh daily using high-quality ingredients, and the facility is described as exceeding food-safety expectations.

Ron's serves the foodservice and grocery channels nationwide. Its retail line, Texas Kitchen, is stocked in major Texas chains including Brookshire Brothers, H-E-B, and Kroger. The company also partners with foodservice distributors and recently announced a collaboration with Center of the Plate Foods Sales to accelerate national growth.

The business emphasizes a homemade look and taste, with attention to detail that extends beyond what can be seen and tasted. Its founding goal remains the benchmark: delivering products that meet global food-safety standards while satisfying customer expectations for quality and consistency.

name: Rooftop Power
old_description: Rooftop Power is a family-owned solar and roofing company headquartered on West Natick Road in Warwick, Rhode Island, founded in 2017. We are dedicated to helping homeowners across Rhode Island, Massachusetts and Connecticut cut their monthly electric bills and build a more sustainable future.
about:
Rooftop Power is a family-owned solar and roofing company headquartered in Warwick, Rhode Island, founded in 2017. The business began with a focus on helping homeowners across Rhode Island, Massachusetts, and Connecticut reduce their electric bills through rooftop solar.

The company installs custom residential and commercial solar arrays, integrates battery storage, standby generators, and EV chargers, and provides roofing replacement and repair—all performed by its own electricians, roofers, and installers.

Its customers are primarily single-family homeowners and commercial building owners in Rhode Island, Massachusetts, and Connecticut who want to lower energy costs, gain backup power, or combine a roof replacement with solar. The firm also services orphaned systems originally installed by other contractors.

Rooftop Power was built to eliminate the coordination gaps that arise when solar, roofing, and electrical work are split among multiple contractors. It offers a single workmanship warranty covering both roof and array, one project manager and schedule, and a single point of contact for service calls years after installation.

name: Rooftop Solar
old_description: Hadassah’s long-held belief that everyone has the right to a healthy environment and a bright future led to her pursuit of a degree in Urban and Environmental Planning. She has dedicated her professional career to helping to create a sustainable energy future, beginning as manager of a land management collaborative of more than 425,000 acres. After developing the skills to run a dynamic solar installation company, Hadassah co-founded Rooftop Solar and serves as its COO. As one of Rooftop’s leaders, Hadassah is able to help to make change at the local level working with a group of colleagues she respects and enjoys.
about:
Rooftop Solar is based in Phoenix, Arizona, and was founded in 1979. The company was co-founded by Hadassah, who serves as its chief operating officer. Hadassah’s background in urban and environmental planning included managing a land conservation collaborative spanning more than 425,000 acres before she developed the expertise to launch a solar installation business.

The firm designs and installs custom photovoltaic systems for homes and businesses across the Phoenix metropolitan area, including Anthem, Cave Creek, Mesa, Chandler, Goodyear, Glendale, and Scottsdale. It partners exclusively with manufacturers such as REC, LG, Panasonic, Hanwha, Solaria, Enphase, SolarEdge, and Tesla Powerwall for modules, inverters, and storage. Rooftop Solar holds NABCEP certification along with Arizona electrical and dual building contractor licenses, and it backs every installation with a third-party 30-year warranty covering equipment, roofing, and labor. Financing is arranged through credit-union partnerships that eliminate dealer fees.

Customers range from individual homeowners to schools, churches, hospitals, historic buildings, multifamily housing, hotels, and office towers. Commercial projects include solar carports, parking canopies, rooftop arrays, and ground-mount systems. The company also assists clients with tax incentives, rebates, and accelerated depreciation strategies.

Hadassah’s founding vision was rooted in the belief that everyone deserves a healthy environment and a bright energy future. Rooftop Solar emphasizes a low-pressure, educational sales approach and a customer experience that extends throughout the system’s lifespan, supported by a dedicated service department.

name: Rooted Furniture
old_description: Great furniture begins with great lumber. We never use plywood or veneer. Each piece is built using sustainably-harvested North American oak. Each board is hand-selected to ensure the highest quality. We also make it a priority to support responsible forestry with FSC® certified, ECC, CARB and LEED compliant wood.
about:
Rooted Furniture operates from a workshop in Boulder, Colorado, where it designs and builds custom solid-wood furniture. The company was established to create heirloom-quality pieces using only sustainably harvested North American hardwoods, avoiding plywood and veneer entirely.

Each piece is handcrafted from domestically sourced species such as white oak, black walnut, hard maple, and cherry. The shop employs traditional joinery techniques — mortise and tenon, dovetail, and tongue and groove — and finishes every surface with a plant-based, non-toxic oil that is food-safe and VOC-free. Projects typically move from consultation to delivery in eight to fourteen weeks, depending on complexity.

Rooted serves residential clients across the Front Range and ships nationwide via white-glove freight carriers. Its portfolio includes dining tables, benches, rocking chairs, cutting boards, and occasional tables for both private homes and office settings. The company also works with interior designers and architects on custom commissions.

A core differentiator is the Planting Roots initiative, which plants a tree through the National Forest Foundation for every table sold. The business emphasizes responsible forestry, using FSC-certified, ECC, CARB, and LEED-compliant lumber, and invites customers to visit its Boulder workshop by appointment.

old_description: Rosebud Wood Products has been in the kitchen and bath cabinetry industry since 1965, producing semi-custom and custom cabinetry for the home.  Many of their employees have been with them for 35-40 years. Their experience and cabinet knowledge has given them a solid foundation to build and grow their business over the years. In 1985, Rosebud expanded into the hospitality furniture industry.
about:
Rosebud Wood Products was founded in 1965 in Madison, South Dakota, as a family-owned cabinetry shop. The company began producing semi-custom and custom kitchen and bath cabinetry for residential customers, building a reputation for quality craftsmanship.

Today the firm operates a 62,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Madison, where it produces a range of cabinetry lines including the Supreme and Traditional series, multi-family SMART cabinetry, commercial casework, hospitality furniture, and closet systems. The workforce includes multiple generations of employees, many with decades of tenure, though the company does not disclose an exact headcount.

Rosebud serves residential, commercial, multifamily, and hospitality markets across the Midwest and beyond, with showrooms in Madison, the Sioux Falls area, and Dickinson, North Dakota. Its customer base includes homeowners, designers, builders, and hospitality operators seeking tailored wood products for kitchens, baths, offices, entertainment centers, fireplaces, and closets.

The company emphasizes flexibility, offering made-to-order modifications to its standard cabinet lines and providing free design services using current cabinet design software. Its culture centers on combining innovative processes with the experience of long-tenured employees, reflecting a belief that quality pays rather than costs.

name: Rubix Foods
old_description: The NEXT Flavor Report is a first-of-its-kind compilation of third-party market research and proprietary data gathered by the Rubix Foods NEXT Flavor Network – a collective of influential taste-making social media creators with Gen Z audiences – who have helped us unveil the unfiltered, unbiased and real-time cravings of this highly sought after generation who will reshape the flavor trends and strategies of restaurant menus in 2025.
about:
Rubix Foods traces its roots to Jacksonville, Florida, where Aaron Block and Aaron Lapin co-founded Reddi-Wip in 1948. The business evolved through the Block family for five generations, with Mickey Block building the first U.S. ultra-high-temperature dairy plant in 1965. Darifair Foods was established in 1981 as the first national dairy supplier, becoming the nation’s largest producer of portion-controlled private-label sour cream by the 1990s. In 2021 the company rebranded as Rubix Foods, expanding beyond dairy into end-to-end product development under continued family ownership.

Today Rubix operates as a full-service product development house with end-to-end manufacturing capabilities. Its 50,000-square-foot Innovation Center, opened in 2022 and FDA-registered in 2024, houses R&D, culinary, and production under one roof. Core platforms include compound butter systems, sauces and glazes, dips/spreads/fillings, performance blends, marination systems, aerosol systems, cultured dairy (sour creams, yogurts), and dairy essentials such as milk, buttermilk, and cream. The facility supports custom formulation from concept through commercialization.

The company serves foodservice chains and high-momentum brands, providing private-label and co-manufactured products for national accounts. Historical customers include quick-service and casual-dining operators that rely on Rubix for portion-controlled sour cream, clean-label cream alternatives, and custom marination blends for proteins and vegetables.

Rubix positions itself on speed, quality, and reliability, aiming to be the industry’s first call for solving tough formulation challenges. Its NEXT Flavor Network leverages Gen Z social-media creators to deliver real-time consumer insights, while a disciplined “velocity to market” approach compresses development timelines without sacrificing execution.

name: Ryco Manufacturing, LLC dba Ryone Manufacturing Company
old_description: The Ryone family has been manufacturing precision cutting tools for the metal and plastic industry since 1972. Originally founded by Arthur “Garfield” Ryone, the business continues to be run by the Ryone family and has a combined 100 years of experience. The business has now grown to offer full regrind services, roll grinding, and machine shop services.
about:
Ryone Manufacturing Company, based in North Providence, Rhode Island, has been producing precision cutting tools since 1972. The company was founded by Arthur "Garfield" Ryone and remains under family ownership, with the Ryone family collectively bringing over 100 years of experience to the operation.

The shop specializes in regrinding and roll grinding services, handling roll grinding up to 20-inch diameter and 80-inch length, and offers a full range of machine shop capabilities. These include CNC turning with live tooling up to 12 inches, CNC vertical milling up to 18 by 36 inches, OD grinding up to 20-inch diameter, rotary grinding up to 16-inch diameter, and turning up to 22-inch diameter. The company also manufactures custom saw blades, slitting knives, and special shank tools in both steel and carbide, and provides full re-sharpening services for those materials.

Ryone serves the metal and plastic industries, supplying cutting tools and machined components to customers who require precision grinding and custom tooling. The business works from customer prints for custom parts and caters to orders for regrinding and resharpening of existing tools.

The company emphasizes its combined 100 years of family experience and the breadth of its in-house grinding and machining capabilities as key differentiators, allowing it to handle both standard regrinding jobs and complex custom tool manufacturing under one roof.

name: S E International Inc
old_description: SE International has been a trusted radiation detector manufacturer and supplier since 1979. Here’s why radiation safety professionals, labs, hospitals, industrial facilities, and government agencies choose Radiation Alert®:
about:
S.E. International, Inc. (SEI) was founded in 1979 in Summertown, Tennessee. The company began with the Monitor 4, a durable and affordable general-purpose Geiger counter that established a reputation for reliability in radiation survey meters.

SEI designs, manufactures, and services the Radiation Alert® line of radiation detection instruments, including handheld detectors, area monitors, dosimeters, survey meters, portal monitors, and multichannel analyzers. All products are built and serviced at the Summertown facility, and the company also provides calibration services and free PC-based and Android monitoring software. Radiation Alert® instruments are distributed in over 100 countries through a global distributor network.

The company serves radiation safety professionals, laboratories, hospitals, industrial facilities, and government agencies across sectors such as government and security, healthcare, industry and manufacturing, laboratories and education, nuclear and health physics, and public safety. Long-term distributors include NDT Supply (since 2000), and end users range from Geiger Counter Pro and Patriots Antiques to military personnel who have used the monitors in Iraq and Afghanistan.

SEI emphasizes honesty, innovation, and dependable technology, with a mission to deliver high-quality equipment that fits a wide range of budgets while keeping safety at the core. The company supports local nonprofits through development grants and donations, and has received statewide recognition in Tennessee for international sales achievements and customer support.

about:
SLH Metals, Inc. operates from Corunna, Michigan. The business traces its roots to 1965 when S.L. & H. Contractors, Inc. began as a bridge construction company. Surplus steel from that operation was sold locally, and the metals division grew until it spun off as a separate entity in 2006.

Today the company runs a full-service metals and fabrication center. Its shop provides custom metal fabrication, precision laser cutting, welding (including portable welding), laser engraving, and a range of forming processes such as rolling, bending, shearing, burning, and hole punching. It also stocks and sells a variety of raw metal materials, serving both large production runs and one-of-a-kind projects.

The customer base spans automotive, manufacturing, environmental, railroad, aerospace, and agricultural industries, along with walk-in clients ranging from hobbyists to local farmers. The company emphasizes its ability to handle complex, accuracy-sensitive work on tight deadlines.

SLH Metals states its mission is to deliver high-quality materials and services at competitive prices with outstanding customer service. It was founded to meet the challenges its customers face regarding accuracy, complexity, and deadlines, aiming to exceed expectations through product knowledge and fabrication expertise.

name: S&S Welding & Fabrication LLC
old_description: We have been serving the community and surrounding areas of Lexington, South Carolina, since 1987.  And for the past 38 years, we have expanded our working facilities, equipment, and working range to include not only the State of South Carolina, but the entire eastern seaboard and beyond.
about:
S&S Welding & Fabrication LLC operates from Lexington, South Carolina, where it was founded in 1987 by brothers Kenneth and Cecil Shumpert after they were laid off from Champion Road Machinery. The business began in a two-car concrete-block garage with their mother managing the office, and it has remained family-owned through multiple expansions.

The company provides comprehensive welding and fabrication services, including MIG, TIG (aluminum and steel), and stick welding, CNC plasma and oxy-fuel cutting on a 70-by-240-inch table, general machining (milling, turning, threading, boring, keyways), metal shearing (up to 5/8-inch mild steel, 3/8-inch stainless), bending (up to 14 feet), rolling (up to 10 feet wide), and pipe/angle/channel rolling. It also offers portable welding via three crane-equipped service trucks, portable line boring, dustless blasting with a rust inhibitor that delays flash rust for up to 72 hours, and powder coating in a 12-by-10-by-30-foot booth with a matching oven. The shop houses a 15-ton overhead crane and multiple welding stations.

S&S serves a broad customer base across the eastern seaboard, including county governments, emergency services, small and large businesses, and farmers. Its project experience spans fresh water and wastewater treatment plants, emergency vehicles, farm equipment, tractor trailers, filter presses, conveyors, fencing and gates, water tanks, and construction equipment such as backhoes and bulldozers.

The company emphasizes a "no job too big, no job too small" philosophy, citing its commitment to detail, safety, and customer satisfaction as differentiators. It highlights its multi-generational family involvement, continued investment in equipment like the CNC plasma table and dustless blasting systems, and the ability to mobilize portable services to job sites.

The company emphasizes accountability: one team, one warranty, one phone number, and crews that are direct employees. name: SEA Wire and Cable, Inc.
old_description: SEA is the largest stocking distributor of Isodyne. We have a tremendous and broad availability of parts as well as the purchasing power to provide you with the best market cost possible. Isodyne’s connector backshell Tool-less Braid Termination System was specifically designed to provide better mechanical and electrical performance for wire harnesses requiring shielding protection for EMI/RFI, HIRF, and lightning. Both the individual shields and the overbraid are terminated at the backshell with one band. Our spring band can be installed and removed thousands of times with no tools allowing for easy re-entry of the cable assembly for repair or re-pinning and no degradation of spring force. The Isodyne backshell system has been in use since 1990 on land, sea, air, and space platforms requiring a higher performance connector backshell.
about:
SEA Wire and Cable, Inc. is headquartered in Madison, Alabama. The company traces its roots to 1970 when Gary Griffin founded South Eastern Associates as a manufacturer's representative firm. In 1982 the business was incorporated as SEA Wire and Cable and shifted its focus to stocking and distributing military-specification wire and cable. The operation moved to the Madison area in 1977 and expanded its warehouse and office space several times through the 1980s. In the early 2000s the company became a small woman-owned business when Griffin transferred ownership to his daughter, Dana Town, who continues to lead the firm.

Today SEA operates as a broad-line distributor of mil-aero wire, cable, heat-shrink tubing, termination sleeves, cable ties, EMI/RFI backshells and related harnessing components. The company maintains an 80,000-square-foot facility stocked with more than 15,000 line items and over 80 million feet of wire. Beyond distribution, SEA provides value-added services including laser wire marking, custom color coding, dyeing, cut-and-strip operations, planetary twisting, kitting, sub-assembly, and a suite of electrical tests such as hipot, spark, pull and solderability checks. It also manages customer inventory through Kanban, just-in-time, dock-to-stock, consignment and other programs, and ships in-stock orders the same day.

The customer base spans military, aerospace and commercial sectors, with named accounts that include Boeing, Unison Industries and Lockheed Martin. SEA's quality system is certified to AS9100 and ISO 9001, and the company emphasizes full traceability back to the original manufacturer, retaining certificates of conformance and test reports for every lot.

SEA's stated mission is to take care of its customers, partners, employees, stakeholders and the warfighter "one connection at a time." Its core values — Service, Excellence, Accountability — underpin a quality program that targets zero defects through comprehensive incoming inspection and root-cause corrective action.

old_description: SINTX is a leading manufacturer of silicon nitride and other advanced ceramics. Silicon nitride is a very hard, abrasion- and corrosion-resistant ceramic solid that’s inherently antibacterial and antiviral. SINTX has been innovating with this material since 1996 and expanded to manufacture other advanced ceramics in 2021.
about:
SINTX Technologies operates from Salt Lake City, Utah, where it was founded in 1996. The company is publicly traded on the NASDAQ under the ticker SINT. Its origins trace back to the development of technical ceramic and composite components for biomedical, aerospace, defense, and energy markets, with a focus on silicon nitride innovation since its inception.

The company manufactures silicon nitride and other advanced ceramics, controlling the entire process in-house from powder preparation through final inspection. Capabilities include powder preparation, mechanical and isostatic dry pressing, green machining with up to 5-axis capability, debinding, sintering, hot isostatic pressing, and quality control. An R&D cell supports compounding, extrusion, and 3D printing of silicon nitride-containing polymer composites, while an R&D lab provides powder characterization, microscopy, and pathogen testing. The FDA- and ANVISA-registered facility serves prototype to production volumes.

SINTX serves biomedical, aerospace, defense, and energy sectors. In the biomedical space, it produces silicon nitride spinal implants and hip/knee prosthetic components with demonstrated antibacterial and osseointegrative properties. Its FleX SN-AP antipathogenic powder is being evaluated as an additive or coating for medical and non-medical products. The company has also secured a supply agreement with Evonik to manufacture a silicon nitride–PEEK compound for AI-assisted, 3D-printed parts.

SINTX distinguishes itself as one of the few firms capable of manufacturing silicon nitride products completely in-house for medical devices. Full control over powder preparation enables tailored material properties, and private-label partnerships allow customers to leverage validated designs under their own brands.

about:
SRC Automotive operates from Springfield, Missouri, as an employee-owned manufacturer structured around an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP). The ownership model ties each worker's stake to the company's performance, a design intended to align daily decisions with long-term quality outcomes.

The company remanufactures gasoline, LPG, natural-gas, and marine engines, and also produces newly assembled and industrial engines. Its shop runs 5-axis CNC machining centers, and a dedicated R&D department operates dynamometer test cells for each fuel type. Every unit undergoes complete disassembly, with all components returned to specification using genuine OEM or OEM-validated parts before final testing.

Customers span automotive, marine, and industrial sectors. The remanufactured engines serve as lower-cost service replacements for OEM brands, while the newly assembled and industrial lines address original-equipment and aftermarket demand. The dynamometer capability supports validation across gasoline, LPG, natural-gas, and marine applications.

SRC Automotive positions its process as distinct from repair or rebuild: complete disassembly, specification restoration, OEM-grade parts, and full test cycles backed by warranty. The company also cites its certifications — IATF 16949:2016, ISO 9001:2015, and ISO 14001:2015 — and a circular-economy approach that reduces resource consumption and waste.

old_description: Auto Rust has been reconstructing rusted cars and trucks since it was founded in 1977 by Jerry Carlson. With a background in engineering, and hailing from the manufacturing mecca of Detroit, Michigan, Jerry wanted to be in business manufacturing products for the automotive industry. Auto Rust's line of SafeTCap
about:
Safe-T-Cap Manufacturing, operating as Auto Rust Technicians, is based in Cranston, Rhode Island, in a 10,000-square-foot facility on the outskirts of Providence. The company was founded in 1977 by Jerry Carlson, an engineer from Detroit, Michigan, who began by welding a friend’s Volkswagen Beetle in his fabrication shop. Over four decades, the team has repaired more than 15,000 vehicles.

The business runs two parallel operations: a service center that restores rusted frames through sandblasting, cutting out corroded sections, and welding in proprietary Safe-T-Cap repair kits; and a manufacturing line that produces those kits. Each kit is built from American-made cold-rolled steel, assembled and welded by certified welders, and designed for installation by qualified technicians worldwide. The product range covers frame sections for Jeep Wrangler, Ford Ranger, F-150, Chevrolet/GMC Silverado and Sierra, Toyota Tacoma, 4Runner, Tundra, and FJ Cruiser, as well as Mopar, Saab, and other models.

Customers include individual vehicle owners, off-road enthusiasts, and repair shops seeking cost-effective structural repairs. The kits are sold internationally via FedEx and USPS, with online sales to the U.S. and Canada. The company’s expertise spans automotive restoration, off-road vehicles, trucks, SUVs, and classic cars.

The Safe-T-Cap line originated as internal tooling for Auto Rust’s own repairs and evolved into a DIY product line to “fix the car without being there.” The company emphasizes domestic materials, over 40 years of research and development, and a specialization it calls “rustorations,” guaranteeing its work while leaving finish bodywork and painting to other specialists.

about:
Safer Textiles was founded in 1975 by Albert Safer in Newark, New Jersey. The privately owned company operates a 180,000-square-foot facility on 5.7 acres in an Urban Enterprise Zone and employs over 125 people.

The mill is vertically integrated, handling knitting, dyeing, finishing, and coating under one roof. Its knitting department produces interlocks, jacquards, jerseys, piques, pontes, and specialty knits from a wide range of yarns. The dye house runs 25-plus modern computer-controlled machines — jets, soft flows, jigs, and atmospheric beams — with lot capacities up to 4,000 pounds and a Datacolor 800 spectrophotometer for color consistency. Finishing includes preparation (desizing, bleaching, scouring), surface treatments (napping, sueding, sanding), and chemical finishes such as flame retardant, moisture management, antimicrobial, and durable water/oil repellent. Coating uses a knife-blade process to apply water-based polyurethane on a 90-foot, 10-zone thermal range.

Safer Textiles serves apparel, medical PPE (masks, gowns meeting Levels 1–3), team sports (antimicrobial, wicking, UV-treated uniforms), military (DOD-spec fabrics), industrial (coated nylon for water/oil repellency), home furnishings, and novelty markets.

The company emphasizes turnaround times, the ability to execute high-volume orders, and a fully stocked warehouse with its own trucking network and global carriers to deliver on time. Its integrated model allows a fabric to move from raw yarn to finished product without leaving the facility, supported by ongoing R&D investment.

old_description: HPP is a unique, non-thermal process that kills pathogenic bacteria  (listeria, salmonella, E. coli ) and spoilage organisms (yeast, mold) through high-pressure, water-based technology. It is a USDA/FSIS and FDA-approved, 100% natural process, and is allowed for use on organic and natural products.  It uses pure cold water, and up to 87,000 psi (6,000 bar) to inactivate pathogens and dramatically extend shelf life. No chemicals. No heat. No additives.
about:
Safety Fresh Foods operates from Glendale, Wisconsin, with a high-pressure processing (HPP) facility in Plymouth, Wisconsin. The company installed a state-of-the-art HPP machine to provide non-thermal pasteurization services to food manufacturers.

The company specializes in high-pressure processing, a cold-water technology that applies up to 87,000 psi to packaged foods for a few seconds to several minutes. The process inactivates pathogens such as Listeria, Salmonella, and E. coli without heat, chemicals, or additives, preserving taste, texture, and nutrients. Shelf life typically increases three to ten times compared to untreated products stored at the same temperature. The equipment also supports cheese ripening control, meat tenderization, and flavor infusion.

Safety Fresh Foods serves food and beverage manufacturers, including dairy, meat, and beverage producers, particularly in Wisconsin. The company works with clients on innovation, cost savings, food safety, shelf-life extension, and process improvements. Its HPP service is used for organic and natural products, as well as conventional items, and is approved by USDA/FSIS and the FDA.

The company emphasizes that its non-thermal method eliminates pathogens to prevent recalls, reduces food waste, and enables clean-label, preservative-free products. It positions the technology as environmentally friendly and a way to improve profitability while sustaining the long-term viability of the regional food manufacturing industry.

Sanel Auto Parts Co. began in 1920 when Benjamin Sanel and Edward Sanel Sr. founded Sanel Auto Wrecking Company in Concord, New Hampshire. The business remained in the Sanel family and, after a 2018 partnership with NAPA Auto Parts, continues to operate independently as Sanel NAPA.

Today the company functions as a multi-location distributor of automotive parts, heavy-duty truck components, paint and body supplies, tools and equipment. In addition to distribution, Sanel runs a fully equipped machine shop that provides custom engine rebuilding for automotive, marine, diesel, powersports, performance and restoration applications, and it assembles hydraulic and air‑conditioning hose assemblies on site.

The customer base spans professional mechanics, independent service garages, individual vehicle owners, body shops, collision centers, dealerships, fleets and industrial accounts. The machine shop serves niche markets such as marine, diesel and powersports, while the body‑shop division supplies refinishing products from Axalta and 3M to collision centers and dealerships throughout the region.

It differentiates itself through a knowledgeable, professionally trained staff, convenient community locations, and specialized capabilities such as the Axalta Acquire Plus EFX color‑matching system, the Axalta VINdicator technology, and a dedicated Sanel Refinish Training Center designed to improve body‑shop productivity.

Sanhua Automotive USA, INC is headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan, serving as the North American arm of a global thermal-management specialist founded in 2004. The parent company, Zhejiang Sanhua Automotive Parts Co., Ltd., is a subsidiary of the publicly listed Zhejiang Sanhua Intelligent Controls (stock code 002050) and began as a developer of automotive thermal valves in Hangzhou, China. The U.S. entity was established to support the company's expanding North American R&D center and customer base.

The company designs and manufactures a broad range of thermal-management components for new-energy vehicles, including electronic expansion valves, solenoid valves, electronic water and oil pumps, heat exchangers, battery cold plates, liquid receivers, and gas-liquid separators. Its core technologies span heat-pump systems, control-valve assemblies, heat-exchange engineering, and variable-frequency control. Globally, the organization employs over 9,600 people, with more than 1,000 dedicated to research and development across four technical centers in China, North America, and Europe, and operates five production bases in China, Mexico, Europe, and India.

Sanhua supplies major automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers in the electric-vehicle and traditional automotive sectors. Its customer roster includes Huawei, Tesla, Changan, Great Wall, BYD, Geely, SAIC, and European brands such as Volkswagen and Renault, as evidenced by numerous supplier awards from these companies. The components serve cabin climate control, battery thermal management, and electric-motor cooling applications.

The company differentiates itself through its early focus on electronic expansion valves, which earned the 2017 Automotive News PACE Award — the first such honor for a Chinese private enterprise. It emphasizes integrated thermal-management solutions that improve vehicle efficiency and extend driving range, backed by national-level engineering centers, comprehensive testing capabilities, and a portfolio of over 740 patents.

The packaging is engineered for cold-chain durability, ventilation, and brand presentation, with documented use cases in apple, berry, and salmon supply chains.

The firm emphasizes its multi-generational expertise and a sustainability platform built on certified forest content, certified sourcing, and recycled materials. The family ownership model is cited as the foundation for long-term customer relationships and consistent service through seasonal demand spikes.

name: Selvaggio Steel, Inc.
old_description: One of the most trusted, family-owned steel shops in the State of Illinois, Selvaggio Steel represents exceptional production capacity, state-of-the art technology, and a reputation for accuracy, timely delivery, and professionalism.
about:
Selvaggio Steel, Inc. operates from Springfield, Illinois, where it was founded in 1957 by Joe Selvaggio after he returned from World War II. Joe, supported by his wife Helen and his brother Jasper, started the business as Selvaggio Ornamental & Structural Steel Inc., building a reputation for custom ornamental ironwork. The company remains family-owned, now led by the second generation—sons Mark and Tony, who began as teenagers on the shop floor, and daughter Michelle, who joined as comptroller.

The shop provides structural steel fabrication and ornamental ironwork, handling drilling, punching, welding, shearing, torch burning, brake pressing, and plate rolling. Its 30-person crew runs a highly automated facility equipped with a CNC beam drill line with robotic coping, CNC angle fabricator, CNC plate punch with plasma cutting, CNC profile and plate rolls, and a 400-ton brake press. Detailing is done in-house using the SDS/2 3D CAD system, and the shop also offers sandblasting, special coatings, field installation, and crane rental with a 110-foot boom.

Customers include healthcare projects such as the Koke Mill Medical Center and Memorial Medical Center’s emergency department and pedestrian walkway, along with commercial and residential builders needing structural steel, stairs, rails, columns, trellises, and custom metalwork. The company’s warehouse supplies raw steel—plate, pipe, tubing, stainless, decking, and structural shapes—in quantities from a single piece to full truckloads.

Selvaggio Steel distinguishes itself through early technology adoption: it was the first Illinois fabricator to use 3D CAD for steel and secured AISC certification in 2007, regarded as the industry’s gold standard. Millions invested in automation have consolidated multiple operations into single-button processes, reducing labor and lead times. The family’s guiding principle—treating others as they wish to be treated—underpins long-standing client and supplier relationships.

old_description: SemiGen was founded in 2009 with a vision of being a multi-faceted and an invaluable partner to the world’s leading electronic device manufacturers. about:
SemiGen, Inc. was founded in 2009 in Londonderry, New Hampshire, to serve as a multi‑faceted partner for electronic device manufacturers. The company operates a 43,000‑square‑foot facility with 20,000 square feet of clean‑room space, housing RF/microwave assembly, automated PCB assembly, and testing under one roof. Now a subsidiary of Naprotek (an Edgewater Capital Partners portfolio company), SemiGen acts as an on‑demand extension of customers’ engineering and production teams.

SemiGen manufactures its own semiconductor and passive components — PIN, Schottky, and step‑recovery diodes, thin‑film circuits, filters, and attenuators — while also providing contract manufacturing: thermo‑compression and ultrasonic wire bonding, ball bonding, fine‑pitch and BGA PCB assembly, and box‑build. Its in‑house ion‑beam foundry offers thin‑film processing, metallization, wafer dicing, and ion‑beam milling. A test lab supports RF/microwave performance testing and high‑reliability MIL‑STD screening up to 50 GHz. Over $3 million in recent equipment investments supports capacity.

The company serves military electronics, commercial products, and medical instrumentation markets, with compliance to space‑level MIL‑PRF‑38534 and military MIL‑PRF‑19500, 750, and 883 specs. SemiGen holds CMMC 2.0 Level 2 certification for defense cybersecurity and earned a BAE Systems Partner 2 Win Silver Tier Award. Customers include prime defense contractors and OEMs needing high‑reliability RF/microwave hybrids and component‑level screening.

SemiGen combines product supply — via its RF Supply Store stocking bonding tools and materials — with manufacturing, testing, and foundry services. Its quality system is ISO 9001:2015 certified and built around military‑spec compliance. The firm emphasizes workforce training, cross‑training, and lessons‑learned reviews to reduce risk on repeat jobs, positioning itself as a supply‑chain link for time‑critical, high‑frequency programs.

name: Service Steel, Inc.
old_description: Located in Huntsville, Alabama, Service Steel, Inc. has proudly provided Alabama and the southeastern United States with quality steel fabrication since 1965. We have even expanded our reach and worked on projects across the country including in Oklahoma and New York City. We are a family owned and operated businesses. Our trained team is always approachable and eager to help.
about:
Service Steel, Inc. is based in Huntsville, Alabama, and has operated as a family-owned steel fabricator since its founding in 1965. Herb Taylor established the company and led it for 40 years until his passing in 2008; his sons Monty and Matt Taylor now continue the business. Over the decades the firm expanded from a modest shop to a 49,750-square-foot operating area that includes a 13,500-square-foot structural steel fabrication facility, with 243 solar panels supplying most of its energy needs.

The company provides end-to-end structural steel services: estimating, design detailing and engineering using 3D modeling and CAD, CNC drilling, and a full range of fabrication processes including shearing, cambering, sawing, plasma cutting, shot blasting, oxy-fuel cutting, precision leveling, slitting, blanking, hot-dip galvanizing, coating, and end finishing. The shop runs overhead crane systems and a CNC drill line, and the 27-person team also handles erection on site. In addition to custom fabrication, Service Steel stocks angles, channels, beams, pipe, tubing, sheet, plate, expanded metal, flat bar, round and square stock, bar joist, decking, and rebar for immediate sale.

Customers span commercial, industrial, retail, education, healthcare, multi-family, government, power generation, distribution, sports, hospitality, convention, and bridge projects. General contractors, construction managers, developers, and individual buyers have relied on the firm for structures such as office buildings, parking decks, schools, college campuses, aviation facilities, government buildings, power plants, distribution centers, sports arenas, hotels, convention centers, and pedestrian bridges. Notable projects include work at Rikers Island Prison in New York City and jobs in Oklahoma.

Service Steel emphasizes its family-owned culture, AISC certification for conventional and complex building structures, and a one-stop-shop model that combines engineering, fabrication, erection, and material supply under one roof. The company states that its approachable team and willingness to handle orders of any size set it apart.

name: Sewer Cable Equipment Co
old_description: Founded in 1959 in Sunland, California, Sewer Cable Equipment Co. was built by plumbers for plumbers. From the early days of the Burton Powersnake to today’s repair and distribution services, our mission remains the same: provide reliable equipment and dependable support to those who keep America flowing. Now proudly part of Hotsy of Las Vegas, we continue to serve the plumbing and drain cleaning industry with the same trust and commitment you’ve relied on for decades.
about:
Sewer Cable Equipment Co. was founded in 1959 by Don Catterall and Jack Bollinger in Sunland, California. Don, a plumber by trade, invented the Burton Powersnake, a rugged sewer cable machine that became an industry standard. The company relocated to Las Vegas in 1990 and remained family-owned; after Don's passing in 2013, his daughter Kristie Catterall Allen and grandson Kirk assumed daily operations. In 2024 the business was acquired by Hotsy of Las Vegas and now operates from Henderson, Nevada.

The company manufactures American-made sewer cables in-house and provides expert repair services for sewer cable machines, jetters, cameras, and cables across all major brands. It also stocks and sells equipment and parts from Ridgid, Spartan Tool, General Pipe Cleaners, Gorlitz, and Warthog as an authorized dealer. Technicians handle drum service, motor and transmission work, and feed assembly troubleshooting, offering both OEM and aftermarket replacement parts.

Sewer Cable Equipment serves plumbing and drain-cleaning professionals throughout the Las Vegas region and as far as St. George, Utah. Its customer base includes contractors who rely on Spartan, Ridgid, and General equipment for municipal and residential sewer maintenance. The shop supports both new equipment purchases and ongoing maintenance for fleets of drain-cleaning machinery.

The business was built on the principle of "reliability, trust, and consistency" — values articulated in early company literature as "timeless principles that express stability and strength during times of rapid growth and change." Founded by plumbers for plumbers, it continues to prioritize dependable equipment and responsive support for the trades that keep infrastructure flowing.

name: Shaker Style Handcrafted Furniture
old_description: Shaker Style handmade furniture by Master Craftsman Stephen C. Barlow in New Hampshire. American furniture maker and designer since 1989 and proud member of The League of NH Craftsmen. Focused on craftsmanship: furniture thoughtfully designed for functionality, graceful appearance, and a lifetime of use. Shaker Style’s furniture collection of beds, chests, dressers, dining chairs, dining tables, accent table and office furniture are handcrafted with North American hardwood.
about:
Shaker Style Handcrafted Furniture was founded in 1989 by Stephen C. Barlow in Harrisville, New Hampshire. A third-generation New England woodworker, Barlow began the business to continue a family tradition of craftsmanship passed down from his grandfather and great-grandfather. In 1997 his wife Cheryl joined the operation, bringing sales and design experience to what remains a small, family-run workshop. The company is a member of the League of New Hampshire Craftsmen.

The workshop produces a line of Shaker-inspired furniture including beds, chests, dressers, dining chairs, dining tables, accent tables, and office pieces. Each item is handcrafted from North American hardwoods — primarily New England maple, black cherry from the Allegheny Plateau, and walnut from Missouri riverbanks — using traditional joinery such as dovetails and pegged mortise-and-tenon. Finishes are applied in a three-step process: fine sanding, multiple coats of hand-rubbed oil, and a final hand-waxed, buffed surface. The operation is built around made-to-order production rather than volume runs.

Shaker Style sells directly to residential customers and interior designers, shipping finished pieces with an optional white-glove, blanket-wrapped delivery service. The company's client base includes homeowners seeking heirloom-quality furnishings and design professionals specifying custom pieces for residential and small-office projects.

Barlow has stated that the business was founded on the principle that furniture should last for generations, not end up in a landfill. The direct-from-the-maker model, combined with a commitment to sustainably sourced domestic lumber and a durable, repairable oil-wax finish, is presented as the core differentiator.

It runs a large array of Karl Mayer warp knitting machines capable of 168–210-inch widths and 24- to 36-gauge, 2- to 4-bar tricot constructions. Four tricot warpers handle fine denier filament yarns (15/1 to 300 denier) including nylon, polyester, textured and flat yarns, low-melt polyester, and polypropylene. A multi-million-dollar modernization is adding digitally controlled knitting, warping, and prototyping systems for rapid pattern development and real-time design sharing.

Shawmut Infinite serves automotive (including headliner fabrics), medical, filtration, military, protective apparel, hook-and-loop closure, and general apparel markets. Its customer base includes automotive and industrial designers who rely on rapid prototyping and digital production management.

The company emphasizes landfill-free manufacturing, reusing or recycling all materials, and maintains ISO 9001:2015 certification. It positions itself as an innovation partner offering design flexibility, precision manufacturing, and rapid iteration from prototype to mass production.

about:
Sierra Packaging & Converting, based in Reno, Nevada, traces its roots to 1924 when Badger Paper was founded in California producing paper bags and wax paper. The company joined Sigma Q Corporation in 1985, relocated to Sparks, Nevada in 1991 as Sierra Converting Corporation, and adopted its current name in 2004. It is minority-owned and operated.

The company manufactures printed flexible packaging for the food and snack industries, offering printed and unprinted laminated films, paper, and foil in one- to three-ply structures. Its in-house capabilities span flexographic printing up to 10 colors on a 59-inch web, solvent-based, solventless, and water-based lamination, wet and dry wax coating, high-speed slitting with laser scoring and perforating, and pouch and bag making on 11 machines. The 170,000-square-foot plant houses eight high-resolution flexo presses from Comexi, Uteco, Windmöller & Hölscher, and Bobst, a full digital pre-press department with in-house plate making, and a quality lab equipped for oxygen transmission rate, gas chromatography, and seal-curve analysis.

Customers include producers of frozen foods, dairy, bakery, deli, pet food, and vegetable products such as steamed green beans. The company serves both branded food manufacturers and co-packers seeking flexible packaging that provides barrier protection, convenience features, and shelf appeal.

Sierra emphasizes that keeping printing, laminating, waxing, and converting under one roof, combined with patented technology and a trained staff, enables fast turnaround without sacrificing quality. Its minority-owned status is also highlighted as part of its identity.

Six Robblees' Inc. traces its roots to 1913 when three brothers—Jim, Bill, and Herb Robblee—founded J.A. Robblee & Co. in Tacoma, Washington. The firm began as a bicycle repair shop before transitioning to racing car wheel work after World War I. By 1920 a second location opened in Seattle, and in 1930 the company was renamed Six Robblees' Inc. after Jim Robblee willed his share to his six remaining brothers. Today the business remains family-owned and is headquartered in Twin Falls, Idaho.

The company operates as a warehouse distributor of truck, trailer, and RV parts, as well as tire shop supplies and equipment. It stocks over 40,000 part numbers across 22 branches spanning eight states (Alaska, Montana, Oregon, Washington, Idaho, Wyoming, California, and others). The network grew through acquisitions such as Union Rubber Company, Motor Wheel and Parts, and several Alaska-based firms. The distributor offers online account management and credit terms to its customers.

Six Robblees' serves the heavy-truck, light-truck, trailer, recreational vehicle, and tire-service sectors. Its customer base includes commercial fleets, independent repair shops, tire dealers, and RV service centers. The product range covers air brake components, axle and suspension parts, electrical wiring, exhaust components, fifth-wheel parts, hose assemblies, and a full line of tire service tools and TPMS accessories.

The business was built on the brothers' mechanical expertise and a focus on wheel-related products. Leadership has emphasized steady expansion through strategic purchases and membership in buying groups such as Heavy Duty America and Ascot Tire Supply to maintain a broad inventory and competitive pricing.

about:
Solar Power & Light, LLC (SP&L) was founded in 2010 in Miamisburg, Ohio, as a spin-off of the Inc. 5000-recognized parent company buyCASTINGS.com, whose management team had operated in the Ohio market since 2000. The company was established by Neil Chaudhry (CEO) and Greg Akers (Business Development Executive) to pioneer Power Purchase Agreements for municipal clients, winning the City of Cincinnati’s inaugural solar RFP in 2012.

SP&L delivers full-spectrum solar services: development (site assessment, PPA contracting, land acquisition, utility interconnection), engineering-procurement-construction (EPC) through SP&L Solar Installers, LLC, asset management (performance analytics, O&M, SREC brokerage), residential solar and consumer services (installation, battery storage, backup generators, financing), and a $300M+ funding engine (SP&L Money Solutions) plus $15M+ in federal and state R&D grants. To date, the firm has originated over 200 MW of PPA contracts, constructed more than 11 MW for public entities, and manages 14+ MW across 29 sites in Ohio, Kentucky, Pennsylvania, Illinois, and Minnesota.

The company serves commercial, industrial, educational, municipal, agricultural, nonprofit, and residential customers. Reference projects include a 500 kW installation for the City of Cincinnati, 55 kW and 80 kW systems for Wangler Ace Hardware and Ace Hardware in Greenville, a 99.5 kW array for Billenstein Family Farm, a PPA for the City of Franklin’s water treatment plant, and a $1.5 million project for Ansonia Local Schools delivering over $50,000 in annual savings.

SP&L differentiates itself through its proprietary Integrated Development Teaming™ (IDT) methodology launched in 2012, distributed inverter architecture for superior low-light harvesting, automated wire-harness manufacturing adapted from automotive production, and early adoption of 1,000-volt DC design to lower balance-of-system costs. As a federal contractor leveraging shared affiliate infrastructure, the firm emphasizes enduring value, innovative technology, and efficient solutions that reduce levelized cost of energy for investors and host sites.

name: Solar Technology Alabama
old_description: Ron Holland is a graduate of Mississippi State University with a degree in electrical engineering.  He worked as a power distribution engineer for the Southern Company for 20 years before starting his own business.  His concern over grid vulnerability and interest in self-sufficiency, alternative energy, and resilient communities led him to start Solar Technology Alabama in 2008.  He built the Alabama Solar Technology Center and has lived off the grid since 2011, allowing him to learn more about independent living than can be learned any other way.  Solar Tech provides custom-designed systems and installation of off-grid and stand-alone power systems, along with an array of different services that support grid independence.
about:
Solar Technology Alabama is based in Eva, Alabama. The company was founded in 2008 by Ron Holland, a Mississippi State University electrical engineering graduate who spent 20 years as a power distribution engineer at Southern Company. His concern over grid vulnerability and interest in self‑sufficiency led him to start the business; he later built the Alabama Solar Technology Center and has lived off‑grid since 2011.

The firm designs and installs custom off‑grid and stand‑alone solar power systems, including solar water heating, solar water pumping, and battery backup systems. Services cover full installation, system sizing, permitting, plumbing adjustments, commissioning, and a paid consultation offering for system optimization. Operations span from Montgomery to southern Middle Tennessee.

Customers are homeowners, cabin owners, and businesses seeking energy independence in North Alabama. Some clients are fully off‑grid, while others keep grid connection but install off‑grid systems for essential loads. The company explicitly does not accept residential grid‑tie projects.

The company says its differentiator is firsthand off‑grid living experience since 2011, climate‑specific designs that account for Alabama’s hard freezes, and a focus on energy security through storage rather than grid cooperation. Consultation services aim to educate customers on system limits and capabilities.

about:
SolarReviews operates from Denver, Colorado, where it was founded in 2013 by Australian entrepreneurs Andy Sendy and Vassie Fitzgerald. The company, owned by Solar Investments Inc., began after the co-founders recognized a disconnect between American consumers and solar installers, setting out to provide resources for researching solar panels, connecting with installers, and getting solar on roofs.

The platform provides a solar cost and savings calculator that requires only a zip code and electricity bill, an unbiased consumer review platform covering U.S. solar companies and equipment, and a matching service that connects homeowners with up to four local installers. The editorial team, with more than 50 years of combined solar industry experience, produces expert rankings and articles cited by outlets such as NPR, CNBC, and Bloomberg. SolarReviews reports having assisted over 1.6 million consumers with their solar journeys.

The service serves two primary audiences: homeowners evaluating residential solar options and solar installation companies seeking qualified leads. Installers can register to receive consumer inquiries filtered by service categories ranging from grid-tied residential systems to battery storage and off-grid installations. The company partners with industry organizations including SEIA, CALSSA, NABCEP, and Solar Energy International.

SolarReviews emphasizes trust, expertise, and privacy as differentiators. Its calculator does not collect personal information, consumers control how many installers contact them, and data can be removed on request. The company states that none of its journalists or editors has a financial relationship with any solar manufacturer, distributor, or installer, and that it drops partners who sell consumer data.

about:
Solid Stone Fabrics was founded in 2003 by David L. Stone Jr. in Martinsville, Virginia, a city once known as the "Sweatshirt Capital of the World." Stone launched the business from his garage, determined to keep textile manufacturing alive in a region that had seen major plant closures. The company moved from a local business incubator to an 18,000-square-foot facility before settling in its current 82,000-square-foot building in 2015.

The operation combines wholesale fabric distribution with a full-service custom printing and cut-and-sew facility. The warehouse stocks more than 90,000 yards of performance, specialty, and novelty fabrics—including stretch, hologram, sequin, velvet, and eco-friendly lines. In-house printing capabilities cover dye sublimation, acid dye for nylon, UV, and latex processes, while a laser cutting department and industrial sewing team produce flags, banners, marching-band uniforms, and home‑décor items such as wallpaper, desk mats, and canvas art.

Customers span the performance‑arts, costume, entertainment, fashion, and swimwear markets, as well as dance and team‑spirit groups, marching bands, theme parks, and interior‑design professionals. The company also supplies home‑décor retailers with finished goods ranging from wall murals to acrylic accessories.

Stone’s original goal was to bring textile printing back to the United States, eliminating the high minimums, long lead times, and questionable chemical processes associated with overseas production. The firm emphasizes low minimums—one yard for stock fabrics, five yards for custom prints—quick turnaround, and clean, domestically produced textiles.

By automating design-to-delivery workflows, the company aims to let distributors focus on sales rather than supply-chain logistics.

about:
Southwest Wire Rope Inc was founded in 1966 in New Iberia, Louisiana, to address demand for reliable wire rope and rigging products from industries along the Gulf Coast. The company began as a supplier of wire rope and related hardware, expanding its product line over the decades to serve diversified markets worldwide.

The company operates three full-service locations in Texas and Louisiana, stocking a complete range of lifting products including wire rope slings, nylon slings, round slings, chain, shackles, thimbles, sockets, and other hardware. Beyond distribution, Southwest Wire Rope provides engineering services such as engineered lifting device design, lift planning, and load testing up to 1.5 million pounds. Its fabrication shop produces below-the-hook lifting devices—spreader bars, spreader beams, lifting beams, lifting frames, padeyes, reel lifters, and custom assemblies—designed to ASME B30.20 and BTH-1 standards. Additional services include field spooling of wire and synthetic rope (under the Haynes Wire Rope trade name), on-site rigging gear inspections using Tessalink software, and lifting gear rentals.

Southwest Wire Rope serves industries along the Gulf Coast and global markets, including oil and gas, marine, construction, and heavy industrial sectors. Its customer base comprises rigging professionals, drilling contractors, crane operators, and engineering firms requiring certified lifting solutions and compliance with standards such as DNV, API, and ABS.

The company differentiates itself through its ISO 9001:2015 quality management system certified by DNV, the proprietary Gold Strand wire rope trademark introduced in 1983, and in-house testing capabilities calibrated to ASTM E4. Engineering expertise is backed by professional engineers who perform structural calculations using Mathcad, SolidWorks, and ANSYS finite element analysis, validated by proof load testing.

about:
St. Johns Packaging was founded in 1954 by René J. Leclair in Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu, Quebec, when the banker and consultant acquired a small waxed-paper operation on the verge of bankruptcy. The business began with fewer than ten employees in a 5,000-square-foot plant serving local bakeries and meat packers. Ownership remains with the Leclair family, now in its third generation, and the company is headquartered in Greensboro, North Carolina.

Today the firm operates as a vertically integrated manufacturer of flexible packaging, producing blown polyethylene film (up to five layers), flexographic printing up to ten colors, wicket bags, laminated pouches, lidding films, and laser-perforated fresh-produce films. Eleven facilities across Canada, the United States, Mexico, the United Kingdom, China, Vietnam, and Australia employ more than 950 people and provide capabilities from extrusion through finished bags.

The company supplies food and consumer-product brands in bakery (bread and bun bags), personal care (feminine hygiene and incontinence packaging), pet food, frozen foods, dairy, and fresh produce. Recent acquisitions such as Amcor's UK bakery business and Australia's Flexible Packaging Solutions have expanded its reach in European and Asia-Pacific markets.

St. Johns emphasizes reliability, flexibility, and responsiveness, focusing on a limited customer base to deliver optimal value. Sustainability is a stated priority: all polyethylene wicket bags are recyclable, and the company aims to reduce both plastic and food waste through economically viable packaging solutions.

The Ostrom family emphasizes that their role is to support the technicians who install the parts, not to compete with them. This installer‑first philosophy, combined with nearly a century of application knowledge, is presented as the company’s distinguishing advantage.

about:
Stark Electronics Inc. was founded in 1938 in New Brighton, Minnesota, as a regional distributor of electronic components. The company serves OEMs ranging from startups to Fortune 500 firms with a line card that includes brands such as Alpha Wire, Conxall, and Orion Fans. In 2024, Marsh Electronics acquired Stark to expand its product portfolio and strengthen its presence in the industrial electronics market, providing Stark with enhanced distribution capabilities and access to a broader customer base.

Through its subsidiary Absolute Quality Manufacturing (AQM), Stark offers custom electrical solutions. AQM produces custom wire harnesses up to 100 feet in length with connectors from Deutsch, Amphenol, and MIL‑STD, as well as cable assemblies ranging from 30 AWG to 4/0 and multi‑conductor cables. The shop also builds terminal block and DIN rail assemblies using franchised lines like Dinkle, UL 508A certified electrical control panels, electro‑mechanical assemblies, and turn‑key panel and box builds.

The combined organization serves the automotive, agriculture, and transportation industries, among others. Its customer base includes OEMs in sectors that require ruggedized cable assemblies for fertilizer sensors, transportation systems, and agricultural equipment.

Stark emphasizes a commitment to quality and customer satisfaction built on decades of experience. The company states that it continuously invests in staff training and cutting‑edge technology to remain at the forefront of the industry, and that its in‑house function testing ensures each assembly meets exacting demands.

name: Steel Plate Fabricators
old_description: Our capabilities include custom fabrication, structural steel, CNC cutting, machining, and assembly. Whether producing one-off components or large-scale production runs, we are committed to delivering on time and within budget.
about:
Steel Plate Fabricators operates from a 140,000-square-foot facility in Knoxville, Tennessee, at the intersection of Interstates 40 and 75. The company traces its roots to 1921, when A.J. Russell and his wife Lucinda started A.J. Russell & Son in an outbuilding of their Lonsdale home. Their son Calvin and his wife Helen incorporated the business as Knoxville Sheet Metal Works in the 1940s. In 1964, their son David and his wife Merle shifted the focus to heavier fabrication and adopted the Steel Plate Fabricators name. The fourth generation, Mike and Anna Russell, acquired the company in 2007, continuing it as a family-owned operation.

The shop provides custom metal fabrication, structural steel work, CNC cutting, machining, and assembly for both one-off components and large-scale production runs. Core processes include laser and waterjet cutting, bevel plasma and oxyfuel cutting, braking, forming, shearing, rolling, sawing, welding (in-house and on-site), blasting, painting, powder coating, and reverse engineering. Machining capabilities cover lathes, vertical and horizontal mills, grinders, and press repairs. The facility houses twelve overhead cranes up to 30 tons, 32 weld cells, two robotic welding cells, and equipment such as a Trumpf 12 kW fiber laser, Cincinnati 600-ton and 350-ton press brakes, a Flex CNC gantry mill, Mazak and Haas machining centers, and a G&L horizontal boring mill. A stock program and on-site services extend support nationwide.

Customers span energy and utilities, biomedical and high-tech, agriculture, transportation (automotive, rail, marine), food and beverage, heavy industry (mining, oil and gas), construction, and government agencies. The company produces structural assemblies, machine components, turnkey assemblies, beam weldments, prototypes, nuclear waste containers, tanks, HVAC ductwork, staircases, railings, and ornamental steel products.

Steel Plate Fabricators emphasizes quality and dependability, citing 95 percent on-time shipment rates and a central location that enables one- to two-day ground transport to most of the contiguous United States. In-house CAD and 3D imaging support 90 percent of projects, and the firm highlights its 300-plus years of combined workforce experience as a differentiator.

about:
Steel and Wire Products Co. was founded in 1929 by Conrad Buedel in downtown Baltimore, Maryland. The family-owned business began by selling hand-drive nails directly to contractors, supplying much of the city's early construction. Conrad's son, J. Conrad Buedel, joined in 1956 and relocated the company to a larger facility outside the city in the early 1970s. A third generation entered in the late 1970s when Mark Buedel started his career; he now serves as president, joined by his sons Reid and Scott in 2009 and later, continuing the family legacy.

Today the company operates as a wholesale distributor from two distribution centers — a Maryland facility in Baltimore (Rosedale) and a Connecticut warehouse in Dayville. The product line has expanded from nails to include screws, collated nails, metal connectors, caulks, sealants, adhesives, and polyethylene sheeting. Steel and Wire also develops its own Bullseye® brand of fasteners. The sales organization comprises more than 25 field representatives and 10 inside salespeople, supported by a workforce that includes employees with tenures of 10 to 40 years.

The distributor serves retail lumberyards, building-supply houses, and professional contractors across the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast, with market reach extending west and south. Customers include residential and commercial builders, carpenters, and specialty trade contractors who rely on the company's broad inventory of branded and private-label fastening and sealing products.

Steel and Wire emphasizes a "Quality – Progress – Service" philosophy inherited from its founding.

about:
Sumiden Wire Products Corporation was founded in 1979 in Stockton, California, as the first U.S. production facility established by Japan’s Sumitomo Electric Industries (SEI). The company operates as a wholly-owned subsidiary of SEI and is headquartered in Dickson, Tennessee.

The company manufactures seven-wire prestressed concrete steel strand (PC strand) to ASTM A416 specifications in uncoated, epoxy-coated, and stainless steel grades, as well as stainless spring wire, stainless medical wire, nickel-plated carbon steel wire, and industrial alloy products. Production spans three plants in California, Tennessee, and Texas, with capabilities including wire drawing, nickel electroplating to custom thicknesses, epoxy coating, and dedicated inventory programs for medical customers. Environmental Product Declarations are available for each PC strand variant.

Sumiden Wire serves the construction industry — supplying strand for bridges, buildings, parking structures, and home foundations — along with aerospace, automotive, consumer, military, and medical device manufacturers. Medical applications include orthodontic wire, guidewires, orthopaedic components, and endoscopy devices. The company also supports durable goods producers.

Sumiden Wire states its mission is to “help Build America” by providing superior-quality steel strand for concrete structures nationwide. Differentiators cited include its global supplier network, seasoned local management, customer service, and innovations such as stainless steel and epoxy-coated PC strand plus ultra-fine wire for surgical catheters. As part of the Sumitomo Electric Group, the company adheres to the group’s Code of Conduct.

about:
Sumner Woodworker Store operates in Sumner, Washington, in a building with roots dating back to 1889. The business has been family-owned since 1996, when John and Joan Schmit — John a former Boeing executive who restored classic wooden boats — decided to open a woodworking store in a property they were renovating. The Schmit family's personal passion for woodcraft shaped the store's founding mission.

The store runs a nearly 10,000-square-foot retail facility stocked with woodworking tools, supplies, and a wide selection of exotic and premium woods. It carries brands such as SuperMax drum sanders, SawStop professional cabinet saws, Robert Sorby woodturning tools, and Colwood wood-burning tools. Every tool sold is inspected, assembled, and tested before it leaves the store. The inventory includes nearly 100 species of wood, plus turning blocks, carving blocks, and pen-making materials. The staff is composed entirely of experienced woodworkers who provide hands-on product guidance.

The store serves hobbyist and professional woodworkers, woodcarvers, and some metalworkers. Its customer base ranges from DIY enthusiasts and small-shop professionals to woodturners seeking specialized tools and materials. It positions itself as a one-stop shop for woodworking and wood carving in Washington state.

The Schmit family started the business to offer a knowledgeable, non-commercialized alternative to big-box retailers. They differentiate by ensuring tools are ready to run out the door, maintaining deep product expertise, and preserving a historical store environment that reflects the community's woodworking heritage.

old_description: Founded in 1995, Sundance Power Systems is deeply rooted in the region and understands the unique energy needs, terrain, and building styles of homes in the mountains and surrounding areas. Our team brings decades of combined experience and a strong commitment to quality craftsmanship, ensuring every system is designed and installed to perform at the highest level.
about:
Sundance Power Systems Inc was incorporated in May 1995 in Weaverville, North Carolina, to expand the environmental work of its founders and bring renewable energy to the broader community. The company negotiated the state’s first net metering agreement in 1996 and helped shape North Carolina’s interconnection policy through Senate Bill 3 in 1998. In 2007 it relocated to Weaverville, where it built a 4,100-square-foot shop and supply warehouse in 2014.

The firm designs, installs, and services renewable energy systems including grid-tied and off-grid solar photovoltaics, battery storage, radiant floor heating, solar hot water, micro hydro, and wind power. It also manufactures the VersaCor, a standardized hydronic heating system introduced in 2002. Sundance serves residential and commercial clients, with a portfolio exceeding 2,000 installations by 2018. Its service department maintains systems originally installed by other contractors and offers annual maintenance agreements.

Customers span homeowners, businesses, institutions, and government agencies. Notable projects include a 600 kW array for Sierra Nevada Brewing’s Mills River facility, solar hot water at Camp Lejeune and Cherry Point, photovoltaic and solar thermal installations at Catawba College, and systems for the Catholic Diocese of Charlotte. The company has provided mobile solar power for the Indigo Girls’ Earth Day concert and the Standing Rock protests, and partnered with Duke Energy on a statewide rebate program.

Sundance differentiates itself through a five-step design process led by Renewable Energy Consultants who avoid high-pressure sales, a service team that works on any brand of equipment, and membership in the Amicus Solar Cooperative for collective buying power. Its early policy work established net metering and renewable energy credit markets in North Carolina, positioning the company as a long-standing advocate for clean energy adoption in the Carolinas.

The company was founded by Wesley Swanson and built a reputation over four decades for custom sheet metal fabrication. In 2007, Keith Williford acquired the business, and in 2021 it was purchased by John Jauch, who remains the hands-on owner directing daily operations.

The shop provides a full range of metal fabrication services including punching, cutting, forming, CNC machining (milling, turning, and routing), laser cutting, spot and robotic welding, roll forming, CNC bending, and thermoforming with custom mold making. Additional capabilities cover prototyping, kitting and assembly, anodizing, etching, powder coating, and electrostatic finishing. The facility houses equipment such as Accurl laser cutters, HAAS CNC mills, a Capital Robotics Fusion Arc 200L robotic welding cell, and Safar Darley press brakes.

Swanson serves industrial and commercial original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) across the United States. Its customer base includes companies requiring precision sheet metal parts, welded assemblies, and finished enclosures for industrial machinery, commercial equipment, and other engineered products.

The company emphasizes direct communication and collaboration with clients, citing its ISO 9001 and UL certifications, certified welders and machinists, and a workflow designed for seamless material handling through shipping as foundations for consistent quality and on-time delivery.

about:
Synergy Renewable Systems, LLC, operating as Synergy Solar, is a family-owned and operated company based in Stoughton, Wisconsin. Founded in 2011, the business began offering solar energy solutions as a cost-savings option for property owners, emphasizing the environmental benefits of renewable energy over fossil fuels.

The company installs grid-interactive solar photovoltaic systems for homes and businesses, along with battery backup systems that provide power during outages and enable load-shifting or demand-charge reduction. It also integrates Level 1 and 2 electric-vehicle chargers with solar inverters, allowing customers to monitor vehicle charging from a phone or tablet. Every installation is led by a NABCEP Certified PV Installation Professional, Ryan Harkins (Cert# 051112-80), and the firm handles all permitting and paperwork.

Synergy serves residential homeowners, non-profit organizations, commercial businesses, and schools throughout its service area. The company positions itself as a local alternative to out-of-state sales operations, emphasizing a low-pressure approach and same-as-cash or long-term solar loan financing.

The firm states that it uses only high-quality equipment from reputable manufacturers and that a proper installation of reliable components is the key to a strong return on investment. It highlights an easy process, quality workmanship, and local presence as the factors that set it apart.
