about:
Founded in 2010 in New Orleans, Louisiana, TCI Packaging operates a 550,000-square-foot warehouse at the Port of New Orleans. The facility is dedicated to the pneumatic bulk transfer and packaging of PVC resins and polyolefins for international distribution.

The company provides packaging services that transfer bulk PVC resin and polyethylene pellets into 25-kilogram form-fill-seal bags and bulk bags (Super Sacks) on packaging lines, running 24 hours a day, seven days a week. It also offers heavy container drayage, trucking, yard logistics, accounting, and inventory management, combining packaging, storage, and transportation into a single logistics solution.

TCI Packaging serves plastics manufacturers and traders who export resin products worldwide. Its customer base includes producers of PVC and polyethylene resins that require tailored export packaging and logistics support from the Gulf Coast.

The company emphasizes a customer-driven philosophy, tailoring logistics to each client’s needs. Its management team brings a combined 50-plus years of export logistics experience, and the firm operates under a Dream, People, Culture framework that sets quantifiable long-term goals, invests in talent, and maintains a proactive, performance-driven culture.

old_description: THACO INDUSTRIES specializes in the design, testing, validation, development, manufacturing, and supply of automotive components, assembly, and spare parts for domestic and international automotive manufacturers and assemblers. Its products comply with the stringent technical standards of global automotive brands and are exported to markets such as the United States, Canada, Australia, Russia, South Korea, and Japan.
about:
THACO INDUSTRIES USA LLC is headquartered in Gardena, California, and operates as the U.S. subsidiary of THACO INDUSTRIES, a sub-holding of the Vietnamese conglomerate THACO. The parent corporation traces its roots to Vietnam’s mechanical engineering sector, though a specific founding year for the U.S. entity is not publicly disclosed. The company was established to extend THACO’s integrated manufacturing footprint into North American markets, leveraging a centralized production model based in Chu Lai–Da Nang City and Binh Co–Ho Chi Minh City.

The company designs, tests, validates, and manufactures automotive components, assemblies, and spare parts for domestic and international vehicle makers. Its capabilities span stamping, plastic injection molding (including a 3,200‑ton press), precision CNC machining, welding and structural fabrication, surface treatment, painting, and final assembly.

THACO serves automotive OEMs and Tier‑1 suppliers globally, with exports to the United States, Canada, Australia, Russia, South Korea, and Japan. It also produces semi‑trailers (skeletal, flatbed, dump, cargo) for North American and Australian markets, commercial and household goods (treadmills, pallets, shopping carts, plastic tanks) shipped to the U.S., Canada, Japan, and Australia, and high‑tech products including industrial robots, AGVs, AMRs, and drones. A notable reference is Ford Motor Company’s Q1 certification awarded to its plastic component division.

The company emphasizes an integrated value‑chain approach—in‑house development, strategic partnerships, and joint ventures—to deliver high‑technology products that meet global standards at competitive pricing. It highlights compliance with ISO 9001:2015, IATF 16949:2016, and ISO 14001:2015 as a foundation for its strategic partnerships with large corporations.

about:
TVS Manufacturing Specialists, Inc. is a veteran-owned company based in Lexington, South Carolina. The firm has been in operation for 45 years, though its exact founding year is not publicly disclosed. It operates as a veteran-owned and operated business, with ownership held by military veterans.

The company runs two distinct divisions. One focuses on the design and manufacture of magnetic components, including air coils, toroids, high-voltage transformers, and springs. The other produces battery cables and wiring assemblies for applications such as golf carts, marine vessels, and material-handling equipment like forklifts. TVS handles pre-production planning, first-piece inspection and test, in-process audits, and final audit and test, emphasizing on-time delivery.

Its customer base spans the golf cart, marine, and material-handling industries, with magnetic components also serving a broader range of industrial sectors. The company supplies both standard and custom components to original equipment manufacturers and aftermarket distributors.

TVS was founded on a mission of delivering excellence with uncompromising quality, a principle reflected in its quality statement: meeting customer design specifications through effective control, employee training, and a commitment that the objective ends only when the product is in the hands of a satisfied customer. Its veteran-owned status underscores a culture of discipline and reliability.

about:
T.Y. Fine Furniture was founded in 2004 in Columbus, Ohio, by Tarik Yousef, a former Honda engineer who applied his precision background to furniture design. The company began with a focus on combining traditional joinery techniques with modern engineering principles.

The workshop produces solid-wood furniture for bedrooms, dining rooms, living rooms, and home offices, using four Ohio hardwoods — cherry, black walnut, white oak, and hard maple. Each piece is built to order using mortise-and-tenon, dovetail, and floating-tenon joinery reinforced with stainless steel dowels, with boards hand-selected for grain and color. Finishing is done by hand with a zero-VOC, food-grade organic oil developed in collaboration with an Ohio State microbiologist. The company operates its own shop within a 200-mile radius of Columbus and maintains two retail showrooms in the Clintonville and Grandview Heights neighborhoods.

The primary customer base is residential buyers seeking heirloom-quality furniture, though the showrooms also carry complementary lines from Stressless, American Leather, Fjords, and Naturepedic. Design professionals and individual clients commission custom dimensions and configurations.

The company differentiates itself through a lifetime structural guarantee, a finish safe enough for nursery use, and a program that plants two trees for every order placed.

about:
Taylor Packaging Corporation has operated from Imperial, Missouri since 1980. The company was founded as a family-owned business and continues as a female-owned and operated enterprise. Its Midwest location is intended to reduce shipping lead times and costs for customers across the region.

The company manufactures custom thermoformed plastic packaging, offering a full range of services from design and prototyping through tooling, production, assembly, and fulfillment. It runs a stock tooling program that includes more than 300 standard cavities and blisters and over 100 clamshell sizes, which can eliminate or reduce tooling expenses and accelerate time to market. name: Tekmos
old_description: We provide companies the best solutions for bridging the gap between standard parts and a completed finished product with the least risk and the lowest development cost. We select the most cost effective process technology and combine devices into a highly integrated low cost device with fast time to market.
about:
Tekmos, Inc. is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Austin, Texas. Founded in 1997 as a spin-off of Flextronics Semiconductor, the company began as a contract design center handling FPGA conversions and large FPGA-based systems for on-demand cable providers.

Today Tekmos designs and manufactures custom analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits, including ASICs, FPGAs, microprocessors, flash memories, and high-temperature chips. The company leverages SOI CMOS processes for operation up to 300°C and bulk silicon up to 200°C, and offers stacked die packaging that combines up to nine different chips in a single package. With over 900 completed designs, Tekmos serves hundreds of customers worldwide, delivering volumes from prototype to over 100,000 units annually for individual part numbers.

The company serves consumer electronics, aerospace, automotive, defense, industrial, medical, oil and gas, and telecommunications markets. Concrete examples include supplying replacement processors for grounded military aircraft, high-temperature ASICs for downhole drilling steering, chips for fitness wearables and oral medical devices, and 60,000 emergency units to restore telephone service in New Orleans after Hurricane Katrina. Tekmos also recreated obsolete telecom ASICs for Lucent switches after Agere end-of-lifed the original parts.

Tekmos positions itself as a bridge between standard components and finished products, emphasizing low development risk, low cost, and fast time to market. Its differentiators include full military lot qualification (MIL-STD-883 and MIL-PRF-38535 flows), ITAR registration, AS9100D certification, and the ability to reverse-engineer legacy parts into modern, manufacturable designs.

Every sale directly funds flexible work shifts for students who juggle academics, athletics, and extracurriculars.

Cordes started the venture to give teenagers real-world experience in customer service, teamwork, and entrepreneurship. The "purpose behind every bag" model means each purchase underwrites skill-building wages for young workers, tying the brand's growth to community impact rather than scale alone.

It also provides long-term operations and maintenance (O&M) services, energy consulting, energy management systems, and energy-efficient lighting retrofits. Since its founding, Tick Tock Energy has installed more than 1 megawatt of solar and small-wind capacity and has reduced several megawatts of electrical demand through lighting and other efficiency measures.

Its client base spans commercial businesses, grain and livestock farms, homeowners, non-profit organizations, and public facilities across Illinois, Indiana, Missouri, Iowa, and Kentucky. Notable projects include a 281.6 kW roof-mounted system for a grain farm in McLean, a 700 kW commercial roof array for a refrigerated warehouse in Effingham, a 604.44 kW ground-mounted installation at a rock quarry in Tuscola, and smaller residential arrays for customers served by Ameren and Wayne-White Electric Cooperative.

The founders frame the business around energy independence, arguing that on-site generation shields customers from rising utility costs and inflation. The company assists clients in capturing federal investment tax credits, Illinois Solar Renewable Energy Credits (SRECs), and USDA REAP grants for rural operations.

name: Tillett Textiles
old_description: Before clients like Billy Baldwin, Albert Hadley, Babe Paley, and Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis discovered Tillett, the British-born Tillett brothers were printing fabrics in Cuernavaca, where their work caught the attention of the legendary Alexey Brodovitch at Harper's Bazaar. Together they founded Tillett in 1946 and moved to the Upper East Side, living above their brownstone boutique and custom screen-printing atelier. about:
Tillett Textiles was founded in 1946 on Manhattan's Upper East Side by d.d. Tillett, a Harper's Bazaar writer, and Leslie Tillett, one of the British-born brothers who had been hand-printing fabrics in Cuernavaca, Mexico. The pair lived above their brownstone boutique and custom screen-printing atelier, where they pioneered techniques such as drag box printing, wax resist, layering, and transparent inks to create painterly hand-printed textiles.

Today the company operates a studio in New Jersey where textiles are still produced entirely by hand using the same methods. Artisans mix custom pigment-based inks and print on linens, cottons, blends, and silks using silk screens — many dating to the 1960s — and drag boxes, a Tillett innovation. The offering spans a readily available collection sold through F. Schumacher & Co. and a bespoke service that allows clients to customize colorways, patterns, grounds, and stripe sizes from the historic archive.

The brand has served interior designers and tastemakers since the mid‑20th century, counting Billy Baldwin, Albert Hadley, Babe Paley, Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, Bunny Mellon, and Diana Vreeland among its clients. Tillett fabrics have been used in the White House, the Oak Spring Estate, and are held in the collections of the Museum of Modern Art, the Philadelphia Museum of Art, and the Cooper Hewitt Smithsonian Design Museum.

The company's stated distinction lies in its philosophy rooted in nature, imperfection, and the artistry of the handmade. As the firm describes it, only the hand can moderate the dialogue between fabric and ink, and customization down to the tiniest detail remains its calling card.

The company produces a wide range of metal packaging including two-piece and three-piece cans, aerosols, threaded bottles, beverage bottles, and slugs, ends, and components. Trivium serves diverse industries: food (seafood, vegetables, wet and dry products), beverages (water, soft drinks, beer, wine, spirits), coffee (ready-to-drink, instant, ground, beans), beauty and personal care (body sprays, washes, lotions, hair products), health and nutrition (vitamins, supplements, OTC, prescription drugs, infant formula), pet (pet food, care, health), paints and coatings (liquid and aerosol spray paints), and home care and industrial (household cleaners, industrial disinfectants, automotive care). Its customers include global brands seeking sustainable packaging.

The company differentiates itself through a focus on circularity—metal packaging that is infinitely recyclable without quality loss—and an Operational Excellence program that drives continuous efficiency improvements. Trivium also offers end-to-end support from graphics and design through certification, compliance, technical consultancy, and training, backed by more than 25 years of experience in packaging innovation.

name: TruNorth Solar
old_description: Since 2009, we’ve been actively involved in Minnesota solar power trade organizations and associations and the only solar provider in Minnesota that is a member of Amicus, an invitation-only national solar co-op with the best independent solar companies across the country.
about:
TruNorth Solar is a Minnesota-based solar contractor headquartered in Roseville, founded in 2009 by Marty Morud. The company traces its origins to a family farm in Bemidji where Morud, along with college roommate Steve and business partner Dave, built their first array for Morud’s father. After buying out his partners in 2013, Morud became sole owner and grew the business into a full-service installer serving residential, commercial, and agricultural clients across Minnesota and western Wisconsin.

The firm designs and installs photovoltaic systems ranging from rooftop residential arrays to large-scale commercial and agricultural projects, and has completed more than 1,200 installations totaling 26 megawatts of community solar and over 110 commercial arrays. A staff of roughly 30 employees handles every phase in‑house — engineering, permitting, incentive paperwork, interconnection, construction, and commissioning — and operates a dedicated “Life of System” service department that maintains and repairs any solar or storage system regardless of original installer.

Customers include homeowners seeking lower electric bills, businesses leveraging grants such as Xcel Energy’s Solar*Rewards and C‑PACE financing, and farms pursuing energy resilience and property‑value gains. TruNorth also develops community solar gardens that allow subscribers to offset utility costs without on‑site equipment.

Morud frames the company’s mission around environmental stewardship and “honest handshakes,” emphasizing that savings extend beyond money. Membership in the Amicus Solar Cooperative — an invitation‑only national network of independent installers — provides collective buying power and continuous best‑practice sharing, and TruNorth remains the only Amicus member installer in Minnesota.

Within months the family-owned business pivoted to manufacturing parts for the World War II effort, establishing a foundation in precision fabrication that continues today.

The company operates as a full-line plastics distributor and fabricator, offering waterjet cutting, CNC routing, milling, and lathe turning with live tooling, custom tape converting, CNC saw cut-to-size, diamond edge polishing, and heat bending. Its equipment includes CNC routers, waterjets, CNC panel saws, a diamond edge polisher, and a heat bender, enabling production of parts from plastics, composites, and metals for both prototype and production volumes.

Tulsa Plastics serves aerospace, chemical, oil and gas, food processing, retail, and convenience-store sectors, supplying materials such as acrylic, polycarbonate, Kydex, specialty tapes, masking films, window films, adhesives, and aerospace laminates. It is an authorized distributor for major manufacturers including Evonik, 3M, Covestro, and Kydex, and machines components for several Fortune 500 companies.

The firm differentiates itself by holding both AS9100 and ISO 9001 certifications, a combination it says is rare among plastics companies, and by emphasizing quick turnaround times and competitive pricing across small-quantity and large-run orders.

UFP Packaging operates from Shawnee, Oklahoma, serving the Oklahoma City area and the broader Southwestern United States. The facility at 8702 N Harrison St is described as a major producer of industrial packaging products, though the company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure in public materials.

The company manufactures custom pallets, crates, skids, dunnage, cut-to-size lumber, and protective packaging materials. Its capabilities include custom wooden crate and industrial crating services, with an emphasis on standardized quality and specifications across its U.S. network. Products are built from recycled pallet components and inspected to meet strict quality standards, with standard 48x40 components and custom cut sizes available.

UFP Packaging serves industries including consumer products, groceries, and manufactured goods, providing pallets certified for industry-specific applications. Its customer base spans operations requiring transport and protective packaging for a range of industrial and commercial shipments.

The company highlights its ISO 9001:2015 certification as evidence of a commitment to high-quality, customer-specific products. It also promotes standardized quality, service, and specifications across all U.S. locations as a key differentiator.

name: US Advanced Medical Research, Inc.
old_description: Hylunia is skin longevity and anti-aging skincare brand founded by Dr. Brian Jegasothy, Dr. Lingam, and Alice Thiel—a team of dermatologists, Ayurvedic practitioners, and cosmetic scientists with over 200 years of combined expertise. Since 1987, Hylunia has developed clean, anti-inflammatory products formulated to prevent inflammaging and help slow down skin aging. Works for all skin types.
about:
US Advanced Medical Research, Inc., based in Henderson, Nevada, was founded in 1988 by Dr. Brian Jegasothy, Dr. Lingam, and Alice Thiel. The trio—dermatologists, Ayurvedic practitioners, and cosmetic scientists with over 200 years of combined expertise—created the Hylunia brand to develop clean, anti-inflammatory skincare that prevents inflammaging and slows skin aging.

The company formulates and manufactures its own product line—including serums, creams, lotions, and mists—using plant-based hyaluronic acid, green tea, turmeric, neem, and vitamin C. Production runs in small batches at the Henderson facility to maintain freshness. The operation serves more than 1,000 professional spas nationwide and has sold over 5 million units to date.

Hylunia products target professional aestheticians, dermatology offices, and spa retailers, as well as direct consumers seeking solutions for age-delay, lift and firm, brightening, oily and acne-prone skin, rosacea and redness, and dark circles. The brand is positioned in the professional skincare, spa and wellness, and anti-aging cosmetics markets.

The founders built the company on a prevention-first philosophy, fusing Ayurvedic tradition with modern clinical research to soothe oxidative stress and support the skin's natural recovery. Every formulation avoids parabens, sulfates, synthetic fragrances, and endocrine disruptors, reflecting a commitment to safety and efficacy that the company says sets it apart.

name: US Wire & Cable Corporation
old_description: True to its name, since 1985 U.S. Wire & Cable Corporation has produced cable and extension cords right here on American soil. This brings an unparalleled sense of pride and commitment to American ingenuity, quality and service.
about:
U.S. Wire & Cable Corporation has been producing cable and extension cords in Newark, New Jersey since 1985. The business traces its roots to 1956 when Alex Folkman founded Flexon Industries on the pillars of quality, service, and family values. Today the corporation remains family-owned and operated under the leadership of Chairman Joseph Folkman, President Warren Swindlehurst, and Vice President David Rauch.

The company operates three U.S. manufacturing facilities and six distribution centers, supplemented by offshore production. Its four divisions — Flexon Industries, Winzeler Couplings & Metals, U.S. Wire & Cable, and Voltec Power & Lighting — manufacture garden hoses, precision metal stampings and ferrules, power cords, extension cords, task lighting, and power distribution systems. Product lines include indoor household cords, appliance cords, cold-weather and oil-resistant extension cords, cord management accessories, and GFCI devices.

Customers span retail partners, distributors, and consumers across the lawn-and-garden, electrical, construction, and automotive channels. Flexon serves professional and home lawn care; Voltec targets electrical and construction markets; Winzeler supplies precision metal components to automotive and other industries.

The founder’s original vision — quality, service, and family values — continues to drive the business. The company emphasizes domestic manufacturing, a customer-first mindset with U.S.-based service representatives, and a commitment to consistent quality and innovation across all divisions.

name: Uniforce Plastics
old_description: Founded in 1990 as an electronics developer, Uniforce has grown into a comprehensive manufacturing partner trusted by OEMs across multiple industries. With more than three decades of experience, we provide engineered solutions backed by advanced equipment, expert craftsmanship, and seamless prototype-to-production support.
about:
Uniforce Plastics operates from Conway, Arkansas. The company traces its roots to 1990 when Uniforce Tech was founded as an electronics developer; Uniforce Plastics followed soon after to provide plastics, tooling, wire harnesses, and electrical assemblies for OEMs nationwide.

The shop combines plastics fabrication, tooling, thermoforming, additive manufacturing, and electrical assembly under one roof. Core processes include handmade two-part fiberglass tooling for deep-draw and intricate shapes, automated 5-axis CNC machining and robotic cutting cells, large-format 3D printing up to ten feet with 48-hour prototype turnaround, and custom wire harnesses up to sixty feet long with hundreds of connection points. Production capabilities extend to automated thermoforming, CNC trimming, and full electrical assembly and testing, with tooling lead times of three to five days.

Uniforce serves OEMs in marine, ATV/UTV, heavy highway vehicles and school buses, and agriculture. Marine work includes dashboards, shifters, cup holders, speaker panels, and iceboxes; ATV/UTV projects cover durable plastics, electrical harnesses, and dashboard assemblies; heavy vehicle and bus programs involve electrical assemblies, large tooling, and custom panels; agricultural customers receive rugged plastics and electrical components built for demanding environments.

The company emphasizes integrated manufacturing for maximum precision, citing fast turnaround (prototyping and tooling in as little as 48 hours), consolidated services (plastics, tooling, thermoforming, harnessing, and assembly in one facility), cutting-edge technology (5-axis CNC, robotic cutting, Delta Sigma projection systems), and OEM-ready direct-to-line shipments with customer-specific designs.

name: United Foods International (USA), Inc.
old_description: We have been a leading manufacturer of both liquid and dry products for decades. From sauces and soup bases to a variety of powder products, items manufactured at our facilities are in retailers and restaurants around the world.
about:
United Foods International (USA), Inc. traces its roots to 1988 when Senba USA, Inc. was founded in San Francisco as a base for manufacturing and selling condiments and spices. The company later adopted its current name and moved its U.S. headquarters to Hayward, California, where it operates a West Coast factory. Additional U.S. facilities were opened in Belcamp, Maryland (2016) and Phoenix, Arizona (2021).

The company specializes in custom manufacturing of liquid and dry food products, including sauces (BBQ, hot, Asian, dressings), soup bases (broth, ramen, vegan), seasonings, batter mixes, baking mixes, and drink mixes. Its processing capabilities cover liquid filling, retort stabilization, powder blending (including Nauta and tote blenders), powder filling and packaging, cartoning, powder granulation, bottling assembly, soft drink production, deep drawing, baking via tunnel ovens, freezing, and tableting. Three U.S. plants are complemented by a global network of facilities in Japan, China, Thailand, Singapore, and Indonesia.

United Foods serves retail, foodservice, industrial, and wholesale channels, providing private-label products that appear in retailers and restaurants worldwide. Customers range from brands seeking custom sauces and soup bases to those needing dry seasonings, breading, and batter mixes for retail or foodservice distribution.

The company emphasizes its in-house research and development team, which handles recipe formulation, ingredient sourcing, and commercialization, and its adherence to GFSI-benchmarked food safety standards (SQF and BRCGS). It also offers natural, organic, kosher, gluten-free, and non-GMO manufacturing, and notes that its varied dry-blender sizes allow smaller production runs without the high premiums typical of larger co-packers.

name: United Premium Foods
old_description: We are full-service co-manufacturer of AAFCO Human Grade and fresh Premium Pet food. Our capabilities range from vet-formulated recipes and palatability testing to high scale production for both raw and cooked premium pet food.
about:
United Premium Foods operates from Woodbridge, New Jersey, where it runs a USDA-, FDA- and SQF 2000 Level 2-certified facility. The company serves as a full-service co-manufacturer for human-grade and fresh premium pet food, while also producing a range of human food products including ready-to-eat meats.

Capabilities span R&D and recipe formulation, palatability testing, raw-ingredient sourcing, cooking, blending, packaging, labeling, slicing, curing, smoking and ready-to-eat packaging. The facility can handle small R&D runs through to millions of pounds per year for both raw and cooked pet food as well as cured and smoked meat products.

Customers include pet-food brands seeking AAFCO-compliant human-grade products and meat processors needing co-packing for sliced Italian meats and other cured items. The company's location in the Northeast Transportation Corridor—minutes from the New Jersey Turnpike, Garden State Parkway and Interstates 78 and 80—gives it ready access to major ports, airports and a dense supplier base, allowing national distribution from a central New Jersey hub.

United Premium Foods emphasizes a proven track record of optimizing the entire production process from formulation to final packaging, backed by GFSI-recognized SQF Level 2 certification and HACCP adherence. Its stated values—quality, collaboration, innovation, reliability and integrity—underscore a focus on long-term partnerships and transparent, fair dealing.

old_description: Unlimited Metal Fabricators, based in Stuart, F, has been a leader in the metal fabrication industry for 35 years. Specializing in custom fabrication, we pride ourselves on delivering high-quality, precise metal work tailored to your specific needs. Our state-of-the-art Trumpf Laser Machine ensures accuracy and efficiency in every project.
about:
Unlimited Metal Fabricators operates from Stuart, Florida, where it was established in 1989 as a locally owned and operated shop. The company began with a focus on custom metal fabrication and has since expanded its capabilities to serve a broad range of metalworking needs in the south Florida region.

The shop provides custom fabrication, repair services, and engineering design support, including a dedicated marine air-conditioning division. Its process lineup includes CNC press brake forming, laser cutting with a Trumpf TruLaser system, waterjet cutting, saw cutting, plate and sheet metal rolling, shearing, welding (with SolidWorks and AutoCAD integration), grinding, polishing, graining, and CAD modeling. The company states it handles projects from single prototypes to high-volume batches.

Unlimited Metal Fabricators serves clients throughout south Florida, with noted involvement in the marine sector through its Marine A/C Division and membership in the South Florida Manufacturers Association. Its customer base includes businesses requiring custom metal parts, repairs, and design assistance.

The company emphasizes its AISC certification, on-staff engineer for design assistance, free quotes, and same-day or walk-in appointment availability as key differentiators. Bilingual service in English and Spanish is also offered.
